chunk_findings.detail: `SystemEnv.get` defaults `default` to `""`, so a missing environment variable and a variable explicitly set to the empty string are indistinguishable. The module docstring says `get` reads the live environment “as `os.environ.get` did”, but `os.environ.get("MISSING")` returns `None`; with this adapter `ddflow.adapters.env.DEFAULT.get("MISSING")` returns `""`. A caller migrated from `os.environ.get("DDFLOW_TOKEN") is None`, or any caller that needs to distinguish “unset” from “set but empty”, will take the wrong branch, violating the stated no-behaviour-change goal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/env.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeClock.sleep` accepts negative durations: `FakeClock().sleep(-1)` appends `-1` to `slept`, advances by `0`, and returns normally. The standard `time.sleep` behaviour this fake is meant to replace raises `ValueError: sleep length must be non-negative` for the same input. A test that exercises a code path calling `clock.sleep(-1)` will pass with the fake but crash in production when the real clock adapter is used.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/clock.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeClock.advance` documents that it moves both clocks forward, but it performs `self._wall += seconds` and `self._mono += seconds` without rejecting negative input. Given `clock = FakeClock(); clock.advance(-1)`, `clock.monotonic()` decreases from `1000.0` to `999.0`. A monotonic clock must never move backwards; this fake can produce invalid states and make elapsed-time calculations negative if a test or helper passes a negative interval.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/clock.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: `clock_conformance` claims to check that “negative waits not at all,” but after `c.sleep(-5)` it only asserts that the monotonic clock did not go backwards. A fake clock that moves the wall clock backwards on a negative sleep while leaving monotonic unchanged would still satisfy every assertion: given `FakeClock.sleep(s)` implemented as `self._wall += s; if s > 0: self._mono += s; self.slept.append(max(0, s))`, `clock_conformance` passes even though the wall clock changed on a negative wait, violating the stated port contract.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_clock.py:19

chunk_findings.detail: The ratchet can be bypassed by direct reads that are not written as `time.time()`, `time.monotonic()`, `os.environ`, or `os.getenv` with an exact `os`/`time` receiver tail. For example, add `ddflow/core/x.py` containing `import time as mytime; from time import time as now; from os import environ; def f(): return mytime.monotonic() + now() + environ["HOME"]`. `measure()` counts zero because `mytime` does not strip to `time`, and `now()`/`environ["HOME"]` are `Name` accesses, not attributes, so `test_no_file_reads_the_clock_or_environment_directly_more_than_its_baseline` passes even though the file reads the clock and environment directly. This defeats the ratchet’s stated purpose and the baseline-only-shrink intent [D-unify].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:count_reads

chunk_findings.detail: The counter false-positives on legitimate injected `Clock` usage when the port is stored in an attribute named `_time`. Given `ddflow/services/x.py` with `class X: def __init__(self, clock): self._time = clock; def now(self): return self._time.monotonic()`, `_tail` returns `_time`, `lstrip("_")` makes it look like `time`, and `self._time.monotonic()` is counted as a direct `time.monotonic` read. A new file using the injected port with no baseline entry would fail the ratchet despite using the adapter.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:count_reads

chunk_findings.detail: The regeneration path writes `measure()` to `tests/ratchets/clock_env.json` without checking that the new baseline is no larger than the old one. If a new direct read is added and the documented `python -m tests.test_adapters_clock_env` command is run, the baseline can grow and the ratchet tests then pass, violating the “baseline ignore lists only shrink” conformance requirement [D-unify].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:__main__

chunk_findings.detail: `Env.get` and `SystemEnv.get` default `default=""`, so `SystemEnv().get("MISSING")` returns `""`. The call this port is meant to replace, `os.environ.get("MISSING")`, returns `None`. This is a concrete behavior change for any migrated caller that distinguishes an absent variable via `is None`; it also contradicts the module docstring’s claim that `get` behaves “as `os.environ.get` did” and the stated no-behaviour-change intent.

chunk_findings.detail: `count_reads` only inspects `ast.Attribute` nodes and only recognizes bases whose name after `lstrip("_")` is exactly `"time"` or exactly `"os"`. This misses direct clock/environment reads that use normal imported names, e.g. a new `ddflow/core/foo.py` containing `from time import time` followed by `time()`, or `import time as t` followed by `t.time()`, measures as 0. The baseline stays unchanged and `test_no_file_reads_the_clock_or_environment_directly_more_than_its_baseline` passes, so the ratchet fails to enforce the “no NEW direct clock or environment reads” guarantee [r-adapters].

chunk_findings.detail: This change introduces multiple adapter families in one change: `clock` (`ddflow/adapters/clock.py`, `docs/ddflow/adapters/clock.md`, `tests/test_adapter_clock.py`) and `entropy` (`ddflow/adapters/entropy.py`, `docs/ddflow/adapters/entropy.md`, `tests/test_adapter_entropy.py`), and the manifest also adds the `env` family. The operator guidance D-adapters-answers says “one family per task” (and r-adapters says a new port touches only its own files). The manifest/file list is the input demonstrating the violation: a single change touches three family homes/docs/tests, violating the strangler “one family per task” rule and increasing the risk of parallel-agent collisions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/clock.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: This change introduces three adapter families (`clock`, `entropy`, and `env`) in one task, contrary to the operator’s strangler guidance that there is “one family per task” [D-adapters-answers]. The manifest adds ports, fakes, docs, and tests for all three families, and this part alone adds the `env` adapter plus fakes for `clock` and `entropy`. That mixes families in one change and in at least one ratchet baseline (`clock_env.json`), making it harder to keep each family’s ignore list independent and to avoid parallel-agent collisions; each family should have its own task/change.

chunk_findings.detail: The documented `Env` contract says `get(name, default="")`, but `FakeEnv.get` defaults to `None` and returns `str | None`. Given `FakeEnv().get("MISSING")`, the fake returns `None`, while the documented `SystemEnv` behavior returns `""`; code or tests relying on the documented empty-string default can then fail (for example, `env.get("X").strip()` raises `AttributeError`). This makes the fake not a faithful stand-in for the default adapter [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/env.py:17 and docs/ddflow/adapters/env.md:5

chunk_findings.detail: The snapshot copy check is incomplete: it mutates the object returned by `e.snapshot()` but then only asserts that `e.get(VAR)` is unchanged. That does not verify that `snapshot()` itself returns an independent copy. For example, if `SystemEnv.get()` reads `os.environ` while `SystemEnv.snapshot()` returns a cached mutable dict (e.g. `self._snapshot`), then `snap[VAR] = "changed"` corrupts the cached snapshot, so a later `e.snapshot()[VAR]` would be `"changed"`, but the test still passes because `e.get(VAR)` reads the live environment. The conformance test should also check that the snapshot is unchanged after mutation (e.g. `assert e.snapshot()[VAR] == "on"`) or that `snapshot()` returns a fresh copy.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_env.py:env_conformance

chunk_findings.detail: `_aliases` records an `ast.Import` only when the imported name is exactly `time` or `os` (`if a.name in READS`). Importing a submodule binds the top-level module name anyway: `import os.path` binds `os`. Therefore a new direct environment read such as `ddflow/core/foo.py` containing `def f(): import os.path; return os.environ["DDFLOW_TOKEN"]` (or `os.getenv(...)`) is counted as `0` by `count_reads`, so the ratchet passes even though the file reads the environment directly. This defeats the stated goal of counting new direct `os.environ`/`os.getenv` reads in core and services.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:_aliases

chunk_findings.detail: The regeneration guard treats an existing empty baseline as “no baseline”: `up = {f: (old.get(f, 0), n) for f, n in new.items() if old and n > old.get(f, 0)}`. If `tests/ratchets/clock_env.json` exists and contains `{}` (for example after all entries were migrated to zero), and a developer adds a new direct `time.time()` call in core, running `python -m tests.test_adapters_clock_env` does not raise; it writes the new count into the baseline. The docstring says the command refuses to raise any number, so an empty existing baseline must still prevent growth.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:__main__

chunk_findings.detail:
`count_reads` counts every load of an imported alias name without tracking rebinding or scope. For example, a core file containing:
```python
from time import time as now

def f():
    now = 1
    return now
```
contains no direct clock read, because `now` is rebound to a local integer before the load. `count_reads` still returns `1` for the `return now` load. With a tight baseline, adding such unrelated code would fail the ratchet even though no new direct time read was introduced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:count_reads

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeClock.sleep(-1)` appends `-1` to `slept` and calls `advance(0.0)`, so it returns normally. The clock port's default implementation delegates to `time.sleep`, which raises `ValueError` for a negative duration. This makes the fake inconsistent with the real adapter and hides the invalid-call path when a service passes a negative remaining timeout under test.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/clock.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: The `FakeEnv` does not satisfy the documented `Env` contract in `docs/ddflow/adapters/env.md`, which says `get(name, default="")`. `FakeEnv.get` is defined with `default: str | None = None` and returns `self.values.get(name, default)`, so `FakeEnv({}).get("MISSING")` returns `None`, not `""`. Code written against the port and relying on the documented empty-string default will behave differently under the fake than under `SystemEnv`, causing tests to fail or pass for the wrong reason.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/env.py:FakeEnv.get

chunk_findings.detail: The new ratchet baseline records direct clock/environment reads in 72 existing `ddflow/core` and `ddflow/services` files (for example `ddflow/core/clock.py`: 3 and `ddflow/services/pins.py`: 11) instead of requiring those callers to go through the new `ddflow/adapters` ports. This violates [r-adapters]: clocks and environment are external dependencies and must go through a port so a change or swap touches one place and tests can use a fake. The baseline freezes those direct dependencies as accepted, so `FakeClock`/`FakeEnv` injected by the new tests will not control those callers.
chunk_findings.title: tests/ratchets/clock_env.json

chunk_findings.detail: `import os.path` is missed. In Python, `import os.path` binds the name `os`, but `ast.Import` stores the alias name as `"os.path"`, so `a.name in READS` is False and `mods["os"]` is never created. As a result, `import os.path\nos.environ['HOME']\n` makes `count_reads(...) == 0`, even though this is a direct `os.environ` read the ratchet is supposed to count. A core/service file using the standard `import os.path` form can introduce or hide `os.environ` reads without failing the ratchet.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:32 (_aliases)

chunk_findings.detail: The `ast.Attribute` branch never checks `node.ctx`. The `ast.Name` branch correctly ignores stores, but this branch does not. For example, `import time\ntime.time = 1` returns `1` even though the attribute is an assignment target (`ctx=Store`), not a direct read. A file that monkeypatches a clock attribute would inflate the ratchet count and fail the test despite adding no read. The check should also require `isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load)` before counting an `ast.Attribute`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:count_reads

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI guard computes `up` only when `old` is truthy. A present-but-empty `{}` baseline is the natural final state after all core/services sites are migrated, but `old` is falsy, so a new read causes `python -m tests.test_adapters_clock_env` to write the raised count into `clock_env.json` instead of refusing. The file doc says the command “refuses to raise any number”; it should distinguish “baseline file is absent” (initialize) from “baseline file exists as `{}`” (refuse a raise).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapters_clock_env.py:__main__
